title: Lesson 7: Final Check and Readiness Checklist
completionTitle: You've completed the OneAccord Digital Standard
keyConcepts: Four questions place any piece of work: a record, internal work, reference or working material, or firm-wide news
Outlook for external parties and formal records; channel posts for internal work; chat for a quick question
OneDrive for solo drafts, never the local drive; the channel's Files tab for collaboration, as the only working copy
The Hub for approved reference; Ninety.io and the Wins, Lessons, Resources team for alignment and knowledge
Every message is labelled [ACTION NEEDED] or [INFORMED]
Handover works when the channel holds the files, the decisions and the open items — not when someone exports their drive
nextTeaser: Welcome to the team. Questions about Ninety.io or the Hub? Ask Abby or Jesse.

blocks.html:
You're covering for a colleague on leave for one week. Three things you need: the approved policy the client is asking about, the decision about the scope change, and the version of the deliverable that went out.

You find two of them in under a minute. The policy is on the Hub where it always is. The scope decision is in the project channel, in the thread, with the reasoning. The third one — the version that went out — is in nobody's record, because it was attached to an email on your colleague's account.

Two out of three, and the difference wasn't diligence. It was whether the thing had been put somewhere the next person could reach. That's the whole standard: every tool answers a different question, and any of them used by habit instead of by question leaves the same gap.

By the end of this lesson you'll be able to:

  1. Place any piece of work in the right tool by asking four questions, without recalling six lessons of rules.
  2. Cover for a colleague — or hand over — and know what has to exist for that week to work.
  3. Write your own one-page version of the standard, in your words, that you'd actually use.

About 15 minutes. This lesson pulls the other six together and asks you to commit to something concrete.

Four questions, in this order

Every item of work in your week passes through these. The first “yes” decides the home.

AskIf yesIf no
1. Does it need a record? A client must receive it, an approval must exist on file, someone must be able to prove they were toldOutlook email, labelled [ACTION NEEDED] or [INFORMED]Go to 2
2. Is it internal work? A decision, a status, a request to a colleagueTeams channel post in the project channel — or a chat if it's one quick question to one or two peopleGo to 3
3. Is it reference or working material? Something someone will read againApproved and finished: the Hub. In progress: the channel's Files tabGo to 4
4. Does the whole firm need to know? A win, a direction, a question worth ten minutes of everyone's timeA Ninety.io Headline for the all-team meeting. Detail goes to #Shared Lessons, #Wins or #ResourcesIt's probably a chat, or nothing

Worked once: a client asks for a revised proposal by Friday. The proposal goes to the client, so it's email — but the draft, the team's comments and the final version all belong in the project channel, and the version you sent stays there so anyone can answer “what did we send?” later. Two tools, one task, decided by two questions.

The standard on one page

When you…Use…
Talk to a client, vendor or partner, or need a formal recordOutlook email
Discuss or decide something with your internal teamTeams channel post, replies in the thread
Ask a quick internal questionTeams private chat — to a post or a call after three replies
Need the whole firm's attention at the all-team meetingA Ninety.io Headline
Draft aloneOneDrive — never your local hard drive
Collaborate on or finalize a team or client fileThe project channel's Files tab, as the only working copy
Look up an approved policy, form or standardThe OneAccord Hub, read-only
Celebrate, share a lesson or find an eventThe OneAccord Wins, Lessons, Resources team
Announce anythingLabel it [ACTION NEEDED] or [INFORMED] first

The one rule behind all of it: use the tool whose job this is — not the one that's open, and not the one you used last time.

About your setup: keep Teams and Outlook running while you work, keep OneDrive syncing so your files are backed up and reachable, and sign-in security is required on your account — IT sets that up with you, so if anything looks wrong there, that's an IT conversation, not a habit to work around.

blocks.prompt: A client emails you a question about project scope. Where do you reply?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. The client is external and scope needs a record.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: External plus a record means Outlook: it is how we reach clients, and it leaves the trail.

blocks.prompt: Four colleagues are going back and forth by email on an internal project issue. What do you do?
options: Keep the chain going so everyone stays informed
Move it to a post in the project's Teams channel
Start a private chat with one of them
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Correct. More than two people on internal work means a channel post.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: More than two people and internal means a channel post — the decision then stays where the next person finds it.

blocks.prompt: Your draft is ready for two teammates to edit with you. What makes the hand-off complete?
options: They have a link to your OneDrive copy
It's in the channel's Files tab and that copy is the only one being edited
You keep the original and merge their edits
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Yes. One working copy, in the channel — not a link, not a copy in three inboxes.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: The hand-off is done when the channel copy is the only copy anyone edits.

blocks.prompt: You need the approved brand standards. Where do you look?
blocks.feedbackCorrect: Right. Approved standards live on the Hub, and an old attachment is a copy of unknown vintage.
blocks.feedbackIncorrect: Approved standards are on the Hub. #Resources and old attachments are not the approved version.

blocks.promptHtml:
Your manager asks you to prepare a client-ready proposal with two teammates, get internal feedback, send it to the client, and let the firm know when the client signs.

Walk through the tools at each stage — drafting, team input, sending, storing the final, sharing the win — and say what you'd label and where you'd put the version that went out.
rubric: Starts the draft in OneDrive, never on a local drive, and moves it into the project channel's Files tab when the team joins
Gets the team's feedback in channel posts with threaded replies, so the reasoning is findable rather than in four inboxes
Sends the proposal to the client by Outlook email, and keeps that exact sent version in the channel
Shares the win as a tagged Ninety.io Headline for the all-team meeting, and celebrates it in #Wins if appropriate
Labels each message correctly — Action Needed for the team's input, Informed for the win — and says what would go wrong without the labels
blocks.coachContext: End-to-end: draft alone in OneDrive and never on the local hard drive; when teammates collaborate, the file goes into the project channel's Files tab and that copy is the only working one; feedback happens in channel posts with threaded replies; the proposal goes to the client by Outlook email, and the version sent stays in the channel as the record; the win is a tagged Ninety.io Headline for the all-team meeting, Informed unless something is being asked, with #Wins for the celebration. Every message carries [ACTION NEEDED] or [INFORMED]. No prices.

blocks.promptHtml:
Different conditions — now you're the one leaving.

You're going on leave for two weeks mid-engagement. A colleague will cover. They've never touched this client. When they ask what they'll need, you realise half of it exists only in your head, your inbox and your OneDrive.

What do you put in place before you go, where, and what do you deliberately not do?
rubric: Makes sure the live working files are in the project channel's Files tab, with the version that went out to the client identifiable
Posts a handover in the project channel that covers open decisions, what's outstanding with the client and who owns what — not an email to one person
Confirms any verbal agreements are written down, because a decision in someone's memory leaves with them
Points to approved material on the Hub for anything the cover will need to quote, rather than attaching copies
Deliberately does not hand over by exporting their OneDrive or forwarding a batch of emails, because that reproduces the problem
Says how the cover can tell what's current — dates, owners, or a single place to check
blocks.coachContext: A handover works when the project channel holds the files, the decisions and the open items, so the cover can read rather than ask. The version sent to the client must be identifiable in the channel. Verbal agreements get written into the channel before leaving. Approved material is linked from the Hub rather than copied. Exporting a OneDrive or forwarding email batches reproduces the original problem — the knowledge stays attached to a person. The cover needs a way to tell what is current. No prices.

blocks.label: Readiness checklist
blocks.instructions:
Confirm each of these before you finish — they're the setup the standard assumes:
  • Teams is open and monitored through your working day.
  • OneDrive is syncing, and OneAccord files are saved there rather than on your desktop or downloads folder.
  • Sign-in security is set up on your OneAccord account. IT arranges this with you — if something looks wrong, raise it with IT rather than finding a workaround.
  • You've opened the OneAccord Hub (open it here) and you know where the approved policies and the sales and marketing resources sit.
  • You know where Ninety.io is, and that Abby or Jesse is the person to ask about it or about the Hub.
blocks.confirmText: I've completed my readiness checklist — continue

blocks.label: Core Takeaway
blocks.title: Lesson 7: Final Check — Your Version of the Standard
blocks.promptHtml: This one is yours. Write the version you'd actually use, not a summary of the course. Your answers are saved in this browser only — they aren't sent to your manager or kept as a grade.

fields.label: Write the four questions in your own words, in the order you'd ask them.
Which single habit from these seven lessons will you change first — specifically, starting with which task?
If you were on leave next week, what would your cover not be able to find — and where will you put it?

criteria: The four questions are in a usable order and are about the work's purpose, not a list of tool names
The habit is one specific change tied to a real task or date, not 'use the right tool'
The handover answer names something that genuinely lives only with them, and a place the next person can reach

coachPersona: You are an experienced OneAccord team member coaching a new colleague through the OneAccord Digital Standard, which covers Outlook, Microsoft Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint (the OneAccord Hub) and Ninety.io. The whole standard reduces to four questions: does it need a record? is it internal work? is it reference or working material? does the whole firm need to know? Outlook email is for external parties and formal records, including announcements needing acknowledgment; Teams channel posts are the default for internal group work; private chat is for quick questions between one or two people and moves to a post or a call after three replies; OneDrive is your workbench and never the local hard drive; once a group is collaborating the file lives in the channel's Files tab and that copy is the only working one; the Hub holds approved reference and is read-only, with changes through Jesse or Abby; the company-wide Wins, Lessons, Resources team is where knowledge is shared; Ninety.io Headlines carry firm-wide items for the all-team meeting; every message is labelled [ACTION NEEDED] or [INFORMED]. MFA is required and is set up by IT. Coach judgment, no prices quoted, plain and warm. OneAccord's values are truth, compassion and service.
